environment.description: Same Node.js 18 application deployed on Ubuntu 22.04 with a custom AppArmor profile 'usr.lib.app.node-service' loaded in enforce mode. The profile was generated via aa-genprof during integration testing and then manually tightened. Profile grants: read on /usr/lib/node_modules/**, read-write on /var/lib/app/data.db (specific file, not directory), write on /var/log/app/access.log, read on /proc/self/**, network inet stream, and deny rules for all other file paths including explicit 'deny /tmp/** rwmlk,' and 'deny /var/lib/app/*.db rwmlk,' for any db file not matching the exact data.db path. The profile uses 'owner' conditions and includes 'deny /** w,' as a catch-all with specific exceptions carved out above it. The SQLite ATTACH DATABASE command requires creating/writing a new file, which the MAC policy will deny for any path not explicitly permitted.
